Morning Brief
Nifty 50 rose 1.14% to 25,514 on narrow participation
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +2.02% weighted by turnover, against +0.12% for the median stock, a gap of 1.9 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

Globus Spirits Limited rose 14.2% on 86 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Schedule of meet”.

BALAXI PHARMACEUTICALS LIMITED rose 17.9% on 156 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “CreditAccess Grameen among 7 stocks closing below VWAP”.

B. L. Kashyap and Sons Limited rose 12.1% on 186 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “BL Kashyap & Sons shares surge 15%, set for biggest 1-day gain since April. What's behind the investor optimism?”.

LT Foods Limited rose 4.7% on 81 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “LT Foods snaps 4-day losing streak, jumps 8% on plan to acquire MK Foods”.

Moneycontrol
Six listed REIT firms distribute Rs 3,234 cr in Q2 to over 5.25 lakh unitholders
Six listed REITs distributed ₹3,234 crore in Q2, taking cumulative payouts past ₹38,000 crore on an AUM base exceeding ₹3.30 lakh crore. High distribution payouts underscore steady rental cash flows and stable office occupancy for trusts like Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield, and Nexus Select. Sustained distribution yields maintain sector valuations relative to sovereign bonds, supporting ongoing institutional capital allocations to commercial real estate.
ET Markets · +2 others
Tata Motors PV Share Price Highlights: Tata Motors PV Stock Price History
Routine stock price tracking for Tata Motors offers no new fundamental information for equity investors.
ET Markets
Connected to your data
Customs should review classification of bulk Scotch whisky imports: GTRI
Think tank GTRI urged customs authorities to reclassify bulk Scotch whisky imports ahead of the India-UK trade agreement. Tariff reclassification or duty rationalization lowers raw material costs for domestic spirits producers, including United Spirits and Radico Khaitan, which import bulk Scotch for local blending. Lower import duties would expand gross margins on premium product categories.
ET Economy
BL Kashyap & Sons shares surge 15%, set for biggest 1-day gain since April. What's behind the investor optimism?
Civil engineering firm B L Kashyap & Sons reported record quarterly revenue of ₹498.15 crore in Q2, returning to net profitability. Faster contract execution generates operating leverage, expanding operating margins and improving cash conversion cycles for small-cap construction companies. Q3 order inflow disclosures will show if execution velocity can offset broader private capital expenditure slowdowns.
Mint Markets
LT Foods snaps 4-day losing streak, jumps 8% on plan to acquire MK Foods
LT Foods announced the acquisition of US-based MK Foods Holdings for an enterprise value of $5.8 million. The bolt-on acquisition strengthens international distribution infrastructure for its flagship Daawat brand, driving export revenue growth and geographic diversification. Subsequent quarterly disclosures of US segment margins will confirm whether the acquired assets enhance overall profitability.
BS Markets
Your themes
Aurionpro Solutions Secures Additional ₹100 Cr Order From Global Hyperscaler For AI-Ready Data Centre In Southern India - Trade Brains
Aurionpro Solutions secured an additional ₹100 crore order from a global hyperscaler for an AI-ready data centre in southern India, raising the total contract value to ₹270 crore. The follow-on order enhances revenue visibility for the IT and data infrastructure provider in FY26. It reflects accelerating domestic capital expenditure by global tech firms, directly driving order execution timelines for specialized Indian engineering and IT services providers.
AI & data centresData centres and AI capex
114 Rafales, 6 submarines! Defence stocks HAL, BEL, BDL shares jump up to 3% - Is a mega defence order boom coming?
The Defence Ministry proposed a 20% increase in capital expenditure for FY28 alongside awarding a ₹1,976.4 crore naval missile-system upgrade contract. Higher capital allocations improve multi-year order pipeline visibility and earnings predictability for defence vendors like HAL, BEL, and Bharat Dynamics. The upcoming Union Budget allocation in February will confirm whether these capex targets receive binding financial backing.
DefenceMint Markets · +1 other
Beyond BEL and HAL: L&T, Bharat Forge, BEML among 5 defence stocks that could benefit from proposed 20% capex boost
The Defence Ministry's proposed 20% capital expenditure hike targets private contractors alongside state enterprise incumbents. Engineering majors including Larsen & Toubro, Bharat Forge, BEML, and Mazagon Dock stand to capture higher-margin sub-assembly and platform contracts. Increased private participation improves execution speeds across complex defense programs, supporting long-term return on capital employed for non-defense conglomerates expanding into military hardware.
DefenceMint Markets
Trump bought up to $265,000 of Nvidia stock in September, disclosure shows
A regulatory disclosure showing Donald Trump purchased up to $265,000 of Nvidia stock in September is a minor personal trade with no financial impact on Indian equities.
AI & data centresReuters Business
US stocks tumble 2% as Anthropic IPO fails to revive AI trade optimism
US equity indices fell 2% on concerns over elevated artificial intelligence capital expenditure and high semiconductor valuations. A valuation pullback in global technology stocks risks dampening foreign portfolio flows into Indian equities. Furthermore, any moderation in global enterprise technology budgets threatens order book conversion and operating margin recovery for major Indian IT services exporters like TCS, Infosys, and HCLTech.
AI & data centresHindu BusinessLine
Capital markets
Jaishankar meets senior Japanese leaders; discusses deeper strategic, economic ties
Bilateral talks between Indian and Japanese ministers in Tokyo focused on expanding strategic, defense, and energy security cooperation ahead of upcoming 2+2 ministerial dialogues. Deeper economic ties support long-term foreign direct investment flows into domestic infrastructure, industrial machinery, and clean energy projects. Listed joint ventures and Japanese capital recipients, including Maruti Suzuki and Hitachi Energy India, benefit from sustained bilateral policy alignment.
ET Economy
Sagar Defence Engineering files updated DRHP for ₹3,412 crore IPO
Sagar Defence Engineering updated its draft prospectus for a ₹3,412 crore initial public offer, combining fresh equity issuance with an offer for sale. The fresh capital will fund expansion in autonomous marine and aerial defense systems, deepening valuation benchmarks for listed defense peers like Solar Industries and Paras Defence. Meanwhile, Mahanadi Coalfields opened its offer to a quiet 38% first-day subscription.
BS Markets · +1 other
Nifty tops 25,500 for first time since February; Sensex reclaims 83K
The benchmark Nifty crossed 25,500 while foreign institutional investors turned net buyers, supported by Brent crude dropping below recent highs and the rupee strengthening. Lower crude costs directly improve gross margins for auto and consumer durable manufacturers by reducing logistics and raw material expenses. Sustained foreign inflows will be confirmed if daily net FII buying remains positive through the upcoming settlement cycle.
BS Markets · +1 other
India allows older vessels into fleet to cut reliance on foreign carriers
India relaxed vessel age restrictions, permitting domestic operators to acquire and flag older cargo ships up to 25 years old. The rule change lowers capital outlay requirements for fleet expansion, directly benefiting listed shipowners such as Great Eastern Shipping and Essar Shipping. Higher domestic tonnage capacity reduces freight expenditure for bulk exporters and insulates local supply chains from foreign shipping line rate hikes.
Reuters Business · +1 other
Macro and economy
Sebi mulls Capacity Building Network to strengthen independent directors
Regulatory proposals for a structured capacity-building network aim to improve boardroom oversight and risk assessment among independent directors. While enhanced corporate governance incrementally lowers risk premiums and governance discounts across Indian equities, the initiative carries no immediate impact on corporate earnings or cost structures. Continued implementation details from the market regulator will clarify any eventual compliance reporting burdens for listed companies.
BS Markets · +1 other
Novartis trims medium-term growth target, shares fall
Novartis cut its medium-term sales growth target to 5% annually through 2028 due to impending patent expirations on core therapies. Lower organic growth among global pharmaceutical majors accelerates outsourcing to Indian contract development and manufacturing organizations, supporting order pipelines for firms like Divi's Laboratories and Syngene International. Upcoming licensing announcements will confirm whether Indian formulation exporters secure generic supply rights for expiring molecules.
Reuters Business
Companies and earnings
Paytm returns to wallet business, will it help regain some of its lost markets?
One97 Communications received regulatory clearance to restart its prepaid wallet operations after earlier curbs on Paytm Payments Bank. Wallets earn merchant discount rates unlike zero-fee peer-to-peer UPI, which could marginally support net payment processing margins. Upcoming monthly transacting user disclosures will show whether consumer habit can reverse structural market share gains by PhonePe and Google Pay.
Mint Companies
Asian gasoline margin plunges to over three-year lows on ample supplies
Asian gasoline refining cracks dropped below three-year lows because regional refinery runs outpaced blending demand. Weak gasoline crack spreads directly compress gross refining margins for downstream refiners including Reliance Industries, Indian Oil, BPCL, and HPCL. Singapore complex crack margins over the next fortnight will signal whether run cuts restore regional balance.
Reuters Business
Geopolitics
India, Japan decide to expedite UNICORN mast deal, key defence pacts at 2+2 talks
India and Japan agreed to fast-track procurement of UNICORN stealth antenna masts for Indian Navy warships. The integrated mast reduces radar cross-sections and will be fitted onto future destroyers and frigates. This integration clarifies execution timelines for warship order books at Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders and Garden Reach Shipbuilders, while potentially expanding system integration work for Bharat Electronics.

Why China's EVs could throw a wrench into EU, UK trade talks
Divergent UK and EU tariff policies on Chinese electric vehicles threaten post-Brexit rules of origin for European automakers. Chinese EV expansion into Europe intensifies pricing pressure on Jaguar Land Rover, threatening consolidated margins at Tata Motors and export volumes for component makers Samvardhana Motherson and Sona BLW. European monthly EV registration figures will track this competitive threat.

Canada sees little US movement on tariff relief, sources say
Stalled US tariff relief negotiations with Canada do not materially impact Indian equities, trade flows, or domestic metal realizations.
